explanation: I searched Mathlib for a statement saying that the image of ℤ_[p] under a ring hom into a field of characteristic p is fixed by Frobenius (i.e. `(algebraMap ℤ_[p] κ a)^p = algebraMap ℤ_[p] κ a`). Checked: the whole `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics` directory (PadicIntegers.lean, RingHoms.lean: `ker_toZMod`, `maximalIdeal_eq_span_p`, `residueField`, `toZMod_spec`, `zmodRepr*` — nothing about powers/Frobenius), `Mathlib/Algebra/CharP/*` (Lemmas, Frobenius, Algebra: only `map_frobenius`, `add_pow_char`, char-transport lemmas — no lemma about `algebraMap` being Frobenius-invariant), the ZMod material (`ZMod.pow_card`, `ZMod.pow_card_pow`, `ZMod.pow_card_sub_one`, which concern elements of `ZMod p` itself, not images of `ℤ_[p]`), `Mathlib/FieldTheory/Finite/Basic.lean` (`Subfield.mem_bot_iff_pow_eq_self`, `Subfield.mem_bot_iff_intCast`, `FiniteField.pow_card`, `Int.ModEq.pow_prime_eq_self`) and `Mathlib/FieldTheory/PrimeField.lean` (`Subfield.bot_eq_of_zMod_algebra`). The closest Mathlib facts (`ZMod.pow_card` transported along a ring hom `ZMod p →+* κ`, or `Subfield.mem_bot_iff_pow_eq_self` plus membership of the ℤ_[p]-image in the prime subfield) still require the non-trivial factorization of `algebraMap ℤ_[p] κ` through `ℤ_[p] ⧸ (p) ≅ ZMod p` (the library itself needs a multi-step argument via `PadicInt.ker_toZMod` and its own `algebraMap_p_eq_zero`), so this is neither a duplicate nor a one-or-two-line special case of any single Mathlib declaration.
